items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that [MATH: \mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2] is an affine transformation. The inverse of [MATH: \mathbf T] (if it exists) is an affine transformation [MATH: \mathbf T^{-1}] such that

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf T^{-1} (\mathbf T(\mathbf u)) = \mathbf T (\mathbf T^{-1}(\mathbf u)) = \mathbf u]

Content:
for every vector [MATH: \mathbf u\in\mathbb R^2.] In other words, the transformation [MATH: \mathbf T^{-1}] reverses the action of [MATH: \mathbf T.]

Content:
Not all affine transformations are invertible. So how can we determine whether a given affine transformation is invertible?

Content:
To answer this, recall that an affine transformation [MATH: \mathbf T] can be expressed in matrix form as

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,]

Content:
where [MATH: \mathbf x, \mathbf u,] and [MATH: \mathbf b] are column vectors in [MATH: \mathbb R^2,] and [MATH: A] is a [MATH: 2\times 2] matrix. We can reverse the action of [MATH: \mathbf T] by making [MATH: \mathbf u] the subject of this equation, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: Au + b|= x; Au|= x − b; A^{− 1} ⋅ Au|= A^{− 1} ⋅ (x − b); I_{2} ⋅ u|= A^{− 1}(x − b); u|= A^{− 1}(x − b)]

Content:
This equation gives us a method of computing the inverse of an affine transformation. Additionally, we have the following:

Content:
> An affine transformation [MATH: \mathbf T] is invertible if and only if the matrix [MATH: A] that represents the linear transformation associated with [MATH: \mathbf T] is invertible, that is, [MATH: \det(A) \neq 0.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose that [MATH: \mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2] is an affine transformation. The inverse of [MATH: \mathbf T] (if it exists) is an affine transformation [MATH: \mathbf T^{-1}] such that

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf T^{-1} (\mathbf T(\mathbf u)) = \mathbf T (\mathbf T^{-1}(\mathbf u)) = \mathbf u]

Content:
for every vector [MATH: \mathbf u\in\mathbb R^2.] In other words, the transformation [MATH: \mathbf T^{-1}] reverses the action of [MATH: \mathbf T.]

Content:
Not all affine transformations are invertible. So how can we determine whether a given affine transformation is invertible?

Content:
To answer this, recall that an affine transformation [MATH: \mathbf T] can be expressed in matrix form as

Content:
